clue.text: Animals let out after another

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed following the cat

parts.note: another animal, following on from the definition: a cat

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the letters of let are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some animals are released one after another from a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' carries on from the definition: another animal. 'out' is the anagram signal for 'let', and 'after' places that result behind the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock such as cows and oxen are animals kept on farms.

clue.text: Meet assistant hosting bishop

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so the helper's word contains the bishop's letter

parts.note: an aide is a helper or assistant
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and meet a helper who is entertaining a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a demand or a hardship is to tolerate or bear it, an older sense of the verb.

clue.text: Cross off culture founded on books

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second, as on a foundation
off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters of culture are rearranged

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, the later books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone crosses out any culture that is based on books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CULTURE into TRUCULE, which is 'founded on' NT, placed above it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means angry, and an aggressively defiant person is angry and combative.

clue.text: It brings up meteoric showers or leaves

indicators.note: showers suggests scattering, so the letters of meteoric are rearranged
leaves means goes away, so the letters of or are taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: A meteor shower or falling leaves seem to be described as bringing something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showers' rearranges METEORIC; 'or leaves' says O and R drop out, and the six letters left make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that induces vomiting makes the patient throw up the stomach's contents.

clue.text: Come down, formerly on drugs from Nepal?

indicators.note: formerly means earlier, so this piece comes before the other

parts.note: someone high is intoxicated, on drugs
to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: Someone is coming down after once being high on drugs bought in Nepal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Nepal is mountainous, so something from there may be described as upland.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal lies in the Himalaya, so a person or thing from there comes from mountainous upland country.

clue.text: Insensitivity associated with large digits?

explanation.definitionFit: Insensitivity is clumsy tactlessness; read literally, the phrase describes having big, weighty fingers.

clue.text: Decline to recognise the Almighty embracing all

indicators.note: embracing means holding in its arms, so the deity's name wraps round the whole of the other phrase

parts.note: God is the Almighty
taken as written
to see something can mean to recognise it

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to acknowledge God, though God embraces everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing all' says the deity's name wraps round the whole two-word phrase, so the name is split into two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that runs to seed stops growing well, so the phrase means to deteriorate.

clue.text: Summon up without one colour

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the summoning word goes round the numeral
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to call someone is to summon them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is told to summon a colour, but without one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: CALL goes round I to give CALIL, and 'up' reverses it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale purple shade named after the flowers of a garden shrub.

clue.text: Reading train ran, with nothing off the rails

indicators.note: a derailed train is off the rails, a picture of disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A railway story: the train ran, then nothing came off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the rails' rearranges TRAIN, RAN and O (nothing) together.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading aloud of a story is the telling or recounting of it.

clue.text: Story you finally printed by one who occupies officer

indicators.note: printed by here means set next to in print, so the pieces run on side by side

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of you

parts.note: a tenant is someone who occupies a property

explanation.surface: A tale about you, printed in the end by an occupier.
explanation.walkthrough: LIE, the last letter of 'you', then TENANT, 'printed by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A military rank just below captain, an army or navy officer.

clue.text: Master given a pound or a penny

parts.note: L stands for pound, from Latin libra
taken as written
D was the abbreviation for an old British penny, from Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A master is handed a pound or a penny as payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman or feudal superior is a master over others.

clue.text: With which you'd cruise around with temerity in the extreme?

definitions.text: With which you'd cruise around with temerity in the extreme?

indicators.note: around suggests moving about, so the letters of cruise are rearranged
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: With what confidence would you drive about with extreme recklessness?
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges CRUISE; 'in the extreme' takes the first and last letters of 'temerity', T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling safe from danger is the confidence that lets someone travel recklessly.

clue.text: Essentially, Royal Society rescheduled party

indicators.note: rescheduled means moved to another time, so a block of letters moves to the other end
essentially points to the core of the phrase, the letters straddling its middle

explanation.surface: Essentially, the Royal Society has moved the date of its party.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'Royal Society' gives ALSOCI; 'rescheduled' moves AL from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering for fellowship and entertainment, such as a church or club get-together.

clue.text: Show the door fixture's edges

indicators.note: only the edges of the word are kept, two letters at each end, so its middle goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A door fitting is shown by its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges' keeps the first two and last two letters of 'fixture', dropping XTU.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone from a job is to show them out of the building.

clue.text: In endless feud, lion and cat mauled jag

indicators.note: mauled means savaged and torn about, so the letters are rearranged
endless means with both ends lost, leaving only the middle letters of feud

explanation.surface: Locked in a feud, a lion and a cat mauled a jaguar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes EU from FEUD; 'mauled' rearranges it with LION and CAT. Jag is Scots for an injection, here used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Jag is Scottish slang for an injection, so to jag someone is to vaccinate them.

clue.text: A girl's after average punishment from Father?

indicators.note: the girl's name follows the shortened average

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl comes after an average punishment from her father.
explanation.walkthrough: Father is a Catholic priest, who may set Hail Marys as penance after confession.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest may impose prayers to the Virgin as a penance after confession.

clue.text: Yesterday, one had

parts.note: read as said on the second of April: a victim of the previous day's pranks, someone who was had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being tricked the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' means tricked; read on 2 April, yesterday was the day of pranks, so the victim speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim of a prank played on the first day of the fourth month.

clue.text: Fresh rash runs out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for runs is taken from the word

parts.note: an imprudent person is rash
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A fresh rash runs out over the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPRUDENT, with R (runs) 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean cheeky, so a bold, disrespectful child is called that.

clue.text: Plot about topless dreamer reached nadir

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the garden word goes round the trimmed name

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden ground

indicators.note: topless means losing its top, the first letter

parts.note: Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream who has a dream

explanation.surface: A plot about a topless dreamer has sunk to its lowest point.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTOM 'topless' is OTTOM, and BED goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the lowest point and stop falling, as prices do before recovering.

clue.text: Rupees and no more foreign currency

explanation.surface: Rupees and nothing else make up a foreign currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The money of South Africa, a currency from abroad for British readers.

clue.text: Stub could result from this row

parts.note: the answer read as an instruction says break up a four-letter word, and its letters rearranged give stub

explanation.surface: A cigarette end might be left after this argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as 'bust' (break) the word above it, and its letters can make STUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a noisy quarrel, a falling-out.

clue.text: Using Vichy water, rub back before chest

indicators.note: the reversed word comes ahead of the French one
back means read backwards, so the letters of rub are reversed

parts.note: Vichy is a French spa town, so its water is French eau

explanation.surface: Someone rubs a chest with Vichy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns 'rub' round and 'before' puts it ahead of the water. Vichy is a French town, so the water is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest of drawers, or a writing desk with drawers.

clue.text: He calculated extravagant leisure is unnecessary

indicators.note: extravagant means wild or excessive, so the letters of leisure are rearranged
unnecessary means not wanted, so the letters of is are removed from the mix

explanation.surface: Someone worked out that lavish leisure is not needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extravagant' rearranges LEISURE with I and S dropped, as 'is unnecessary' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler, the eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician famous for his calculations.

clue.text: Couple played ludo (pub game's final)

indicators.note: played means performed in a new way, so the letters are rearranged
final picks out the last letter of game's

explanation.surface: A couple played ludo, a board game, in a pub as the final game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges LUDO, PUB and E, the 'final' letter of 'game's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair up or share with someone, as two people joining together.

clue.text: Detachment upheld by English couple

indicators.note: in a down clue, this piece sits above the next one, held up by it

parts.note: a detachment is a military unit

explanation.surface: A military detachment is supported by an English pair.
explanation.walkthrough: In the down entry UNIT is 'upheld by' E, sitting on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join or link them together.

clue.text: Man dictated letters

indicators.note: dictated means spoken out for someone to write down, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A man spoke his letters out loud for a secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Post consists of the letters delivered to a house.

clue.text: Heartless critic on tele's up for full dose of E?

indicators.note: up means in turmoil, so the letters are rearranged
heartless removes the middle of critic, its two central letters

parts.note: the 's means is, so the word is just tele

explanation.surface: A heartless critic says television is up for a full dose of ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' turns CRITIC into CRIC, and 'up' rearranges it with ON and TELE. The prefix e- in email is short for the answer, its full form.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter E in email or ebook stands for this word in full.

clue.text: Duster shaken without it leaves debris

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the shuffled letters go round the next word
shaken means disturbed, so the letters of duster are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duster, shaken without it, leaves debris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' rearranges 'Duster', and 'without' here means outside, not lacking: the shuffled letters go round 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragments and rubbish left over after something breaks up.

clue.text: At coup's conclusion, rifle shot's appropriate

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter
shot means broken or ruined, so the letters of rifle are rearranged

explanation.surface: When a coup ends, firing a rifle is fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: P ends 'coup's'; 'shot' rearranges RIFLE. 'appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for oneself without right, to steal it.
